name: Mahmoud Ahmadinejad
role: President of Iran (2005–2013); mayor of Tehran (2003–2005)
summary: Ahmadinejad is an Iranian populist and Shia Islamist conservative who combined welfare transfers, housing and price interventions for poorer Iranians with hostility to capitalism and Western domination. He backed Iran's nuclear programme while denying it sought a bomb, rejected Israel's legitimacy, questioned the Holocaust, and promoted a larger population and traditional family. After leaving office he clashed with Iran's establishment, calling for free elections and criticising corruption.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He called capitalism a failed model at the UN (2012), and at home he intervened in prices and set interest rates by decree rather than leaving them to markets.

cut-welfare.rationale: His record expanded transfers: a monthly cash payment replacing subsidies, newborn payments and justice shares for lower-income Iranians; he never argued that welfare breeds dependency.

surveillance-ok.rationale: He said governments invent enemies and use fear of terrorism to wiretap and control their own people and told Bush not to bug citizens' phone calls.

legalize-drugs.rationale: He defended capital punishment for illicit drug traffickers in Iran, which implies he supports their activity being illegal; he did not discuss legalising adult use.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: He criticised laws that jail or fine people who research historical events, but also objected to speech that offends sacred beliefs.

traditional-family.rationale: He called the family the noblest institution of societies, said it had been weakened.

more-religion-public.rationale: His letter to Bush said a return to the teachings of the divine prophets is the only road to salvation, and he tied officeholding to the prophets' tradition.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He said powers try to eliminate indigenous cultures to strip nations of identity and called pure indigenous cultures a source of diversity under attack.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He wanted the UN restructured, saying it lacked efficiency, but he also rejected Security Council measures and treated IAEA findings as politicised.

nation-first.rationale: He presented Iran as committed to harmony, cooperation and joint global management rather than putting national interest first.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He said the war on Iraq was waged on a pretext and that spreading democracy through war from outside is impossible.

expand-nuclear.rationale: He drove Iran's enrichment programme and defended the right to peaceful nuclear technology for power plants.

revolution-justified.rationale: He defended the 1979 revolution as a natural, mostly peaceful reaction to a cruel regime and defended the students' embassy takeover as natural.

basic-income.rationale: He drove replacing price subsidies with monthly cash payments to citizens, but it compensated price rises and was not described as a basic income.

widespread-small-property.rationale: His justice shares plan distributed ownership of state firms to millions of lower-income families through cooperatives.

separate-church-state.rationale: He wished for pious and pure scholars to run the world under a pious ruler, and led an Islamic Republic; he did not argue for a wall between religion and state.

self-interest-moral.rationale: He blamed selfishness, egoism and carnal desires for wrongdoing and said purity requires freeing the heart of selfishness.

limit-population.rationale: He told MPs he wanted to scrap birth-control policies, said he opposed 'two children are enough' and argued Iran could hold 120 million people.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He said Iran does not want to rule over other people's land and seeks no influence or domination.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: He told CBS that Israel is not a nation, called it a regime imposed on Palestine and urged that its backers stop supporting it or that all Palestinians decide by referendum.

national-self-determination.rationale: He repeatedly argued for self-determination of Palestinians, Iraqis and Iranians, including a free vote for all Palestinians on their fate.

force-without-un.rationale: He listed unilateralism and imposed wars among the world's ills and said Iran has never been an aggressor.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He argued that science is light given by God, that limiting it to experimental fields is oppression, and that knowledge must be joined with piety.

dominated-front.rationale: He urged nations to stand together against the acquisitive minority and hosted the 2012 Non-Aligned Movement summit, which he presented as rejecting the unjust world order.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: He said women should work less to devote time to their main mission of raising children and proposed shorter hours tied to number of children.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He said Western election money is an investment that leaves ordinary voices unheard, and after leaving office he criticised corruption and judicial injustice in Iran.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He called for an order in which everybody is equal before the law without double standards, and said all peoples deserve dignity.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: He described Israel as built by emigrants from distant countries who pushed Palestinians out as refugees and as an imposed regime.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He called authority a gift from the people to rulers and later wrote that self-determination is the people's fundamental right, calling for free elections.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: He denounced the survival-of-the-fittest theory as a justification for inhuman actions and criticised capitalist 'unhealthy and devastating competition'.

priority-to-poor.rationale: His letter asked whether leaders defend the underprivileged, and he allotted justice shares to the lowest-income third of Iranians.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: He said Iran has room for many more people and blamed poverty on the world order and its colonial roots, not on population growth.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: As president he used price interventions on goods, cement and services; 50 economists criticised them in 2006 and he rejected the criticism.

death-penalty.rationale: Asked at Columbia he defended capital punishment in Iran for drug traffickers and people who violate others' rights, and compared it with US practice.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: His letter to Bush argued that military spending should instead fund investment and assistance to poor countries and said Africa's wealth had been looted.

central-bank-independence.rationale: He cut interest rates by presidential decree to below inflation instead of leaving them to the central bank.

refugee-return.rationale: He noted millions of displaced Palestinians and wrote that original inhabitants inside and outside Palestine should decide their fate.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He said Iraqis have no need for a guardian and can run their own affairs, and that regional peoples know how to manage themselves.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: He said capitalism is bogged down in a self-made quagmire and has reached a deadlock, with no real solutions to current problems.

delink-world-market.rationale: In 2024 he promised constructive engagement with the world and better economic relations with all nations.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: He argued that poverty is imposed on nations by an order built on colonialism and that Africa's wealth is looted; he did not frame this as a surplus-transfer theory.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: He said human values should be the measure of dignity in place of affluence and consumerism, and that consumption-driven economies serve only a few countries.

corporate-influence.rationale: He said big campaign spending in capitalist countries is an investment and that parties represent few people.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: He backed a payment for each newborn and called for a baby boom, framing growth in Iran's population as a strength; he did not discuss immigration.

non-intervention.rationale: He condemned the invasion of Iraq and said democracy cannot be brought from outside through war; he did not state an absolute rule.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: He rejected domination by a single power and the Security Council veto as discrimination and called the current order unjust.

religion-illusion.rationale: He called the Almighty the greatest and clearest reality and said all beings are signs of God's existence.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He called capitalism a system founded on materialism and in a deadlock and a failed model; he did not address its historical role in building productive capacity.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: At the UN in 2012 he said Marxism is no longer around and capitalism is deadlocked, and called for a new order built on faith, justice and human dignity.

holocaust-denial.rationale: He called the Holocaust a myth in 2005, hosted a conference on it and in 2013 praised promoting that doubt; in interviews he also said 'assuming it happened', so he mostly cast doubt.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: As host of the Non-Aligned Movement summit he said NAM was right to reject the poles of power.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: He described the world's power centres as having entrusted themselves to the Devil and urged believers to fight the unjust order with trust in God.

person-over-state.rationale: He said world leaders should regard themselves as committed servants of their people, not their superiors.

spiritual-nature.rationale: He said the human being is a combination of material and spirit and that spirit supersedes the physical side; he asked for an order serving both.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He said Iran never attacked another nation, wants peace and is strong enough to defend itself.

arms-reduction.rationale: He said Iran seeks a world movement toward nuclear disarmament and wished that arms could be turned into pens and military money into welfare.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He told the UN that international economic institutions were pressured and unfair and that a new order was needed, naming UN and economic reform as aims.

shared-human-nature.rationale: He described humans as one essence and as God's supreme creature with a pure divine nature, on which he based dignity.

religions-one-truth.rationale: He wrote that all divine religions share the one word of monotheism and said the God of all peoples is one, though he spoke of divine religions only.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: He proposed a free referendum of all Palestinian citizens, Muslim, Christian and Jewish, to settle their fate.

national-resource-control.rationale: He said Iraqis and Africans should be able to use their own resources, and criticised foreign looting of Africa's minerals.

multipolar-world.rationale: He said the era of world empires has ended and that NAM rejected rule by poles of power and unbridled hegemony; his own proposal was joint global management.

notes: Living: Wikipedia and 2026 press reports (conflicting reports of death in March 2026 were denied; he was reported seen in July 2026). Views on economics were mixed (privatisation to the poor via justice shares alongside price controls and subsidies), so economy answers are limited to clear measures. Interview and speech items are treated as his own words even when translated. Where he never addressed a topic (healthcare, abortion, taxes, climate policy) the answer is null.
